newsitem.title: JAPAN: FORECAST - Japan September money growth seen steady.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Japan September money growth seen steady.

text.p: Japan's broadly defined money supply average of M2 plus certificates of deposit (M2+CDs), the key gauge of money supply, is expected to be steady in September compared with August, economists said on Tuesday.

"The growth is expected to be somewhere between 3.6 and 3.7 percent. The trend has not changed for the past several months and we're not likely to see much of a surprise," said Mamoru Yamaguchi, an economist at Nikko Research Center.
Economists polled by Reuters in Tokyo gave predictions of growth of around 3.6 percent to 3.7 percent. In August, money supply grew a preliminary 3.7 percent from a year earlier.
The data will be released at 11 a.m. (0200 GMT) on Thursday.
Economists said money supply growth was expected to be on a downward trend in the longer term as bank lending to private corporations remains extremely sluggish.
"There are no convincing signs that show an increase in lending," Nikko's Yamaguchi said. "If this trend lasts longer then we'll eventually see the money supply growth peaking out."
An economist at Daiwa Bank Research Institute said housing loan demand from individuals had also peaked out, which was another factor to keep lending by city banks generally low.
Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan +3.6 percent
